title: Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models
summary: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) can induce behaviors beyond those explicitly targeted. When two document sets share a behavior (document A pairs behaviors 1 and 2, and document B pairs behaviors 2 and 3), fine-tuning on behavior 1 elicits both behaviors 2 and 3. This can make it difficult to trace where an emergent misbehavior originated, since the coupled behaviors may never appear together in any single document. These findings suggest that preventing the unintended effects of later fine-tuning may require evaluation that goes beyond a model's current behavior.
